audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill for levels 1-6 and Skill again at two items, while the content win[] rows and the packet levelChart read Orianna five times then Azir twice — six of seven rows rendering two answers.
audit.why: Command: Attack is 815 range on 7/6/5/4/3s against Azir's 740-range Q on 14/12/10/8/6s, and the ball remains where it lands. Orianna out-cycles Azir's poke by better than two to one before items, which is the whole early lane; Nashor's is where it turns.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side moved to Orianna with all five whys rewritten, and phases[6].side moved to Azir where its why already described Azir winning.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named no Orianna ability and no number: 'level 6 adds dive insurance' against a champion who does not dive.
audit.why: Orianna's spikes are Command: Attack falling from 7s to 3s and Command: Shockwave at 6 (410 range, 110/95/80s). Azir's are Nashor's Tooth and Emperor's Divide, which matters here as the tool that breaks up the pile Shockwave gathers rather than as anti-dive.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text, breakdown.spikes, whys[4] and the content mid text rewritten around those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'track the ball position like a second enemy' four separate times without once saying what the ball does. It never stated that Shockwave launches enemies TOWARD the ball, that its range is only 410, or that Command: Protect can send the ball to any ally at 1095 range — which is how a Shockwave arrives from a flank.
audit.why: Enemy R text: 'launching nearby enemies towards the Ball after a short delay', 410 range, 110/95/80s. Enemy E: 1095 range, 9s, attaches the ball to an allied champion, shields them, damages enemies it passes through and grants them Armor and MR. Enemy Q: 815 range, 7/6/5/4/3s, 'Her Ball remains at the target location after' — which is the sequencing lever Azir has, because she is disarmed wherever the ball is not.
audit.corrected: The pull direction, the 410 radius, the E-to-ally delivery and the ball-stays-where-it-lands rule are now all stated, and the last one carries the trading and wave advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: sequencingCues 0 — nowhere on the page was there a concrete 'wait for X, then Y' line, and breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit.
audit.why: Command: Attack leaves the ball at the target location and is 7s at rank 1, so the moment she throws it into the wave is a countable window. Shockwave is 110s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave and the content early text now all carry the same concrete sequence: step up when she Qs the wave, leave before the Q returns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wave advice was generic ('the crash is a timer you set') and used the wrong pronoun for her tower.
audit.why: A frozen wave under her tower is where she parks a stationary ball, so every last-hit is taxed.
audit.corrected: Crash timing now keyed to her Q leaving the ball stranded in the minions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Orianna addressed as he/his/him in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, loading, breakdown.wave, two dosFull titles and four report entries.
audit.corrected: All corrected in the proposed strings.

edits.before: Orianna's ball gives her both poke and zoning that outclass your immobile, cooldown-heavy kit in this window, so track her ball's position carefully and avoid standing in its threat range. She wins straightforward trades here, so prioritize safe soldier farming over contesting her directly. Watch for jungle ganks that pair with her ball-slow for a kill setup.
edits.after: Command: Attack reaches 815 on a 7-second cooldown while your Q is 14, so you lose any straight poke war — farm behind soldiers instead. The ball stays where it lands, and that is your sequencing rule: step to soldier range the moment she throws it into the wave, and leave before it comes back. Watch for ganks paired with her Command: Dissonance slow field.

edits.before: Her ultimate Shockwave is one of the best teamfight tools in the game and can single-handedly flip a fight if she catches your team grouped, so respect her all-in and skirmish potential even after your own R comes online at 6. Your R does give you a way to disengage or wall off her ball's approach, softening the threat. Focus on wave management and safe rotations rather than direct duels in this stretch.
edits.after: Shockwave launches everyone within 410 of the ball toward it after a short delay, so where the ball sits tells you exactly which way your team is about to be thrown — never group tighter than that radius. It is 110 seconds at rank 1, and that spent minute is the only stretch where grouping is free. Emperor's Divide answers the follow-up rather than the pull itself. Play waves and rotations, not duels.

edits.before: Once you have your first item your poke and clear start to match her ball-based zoning, and by two items your zone control and R give you the tools to counter her Shockwave setup by walling off approach angles or disengaging before she can detonate it. Build MR if she's snowballed a lead (Abyssal Mask), since her burst-and-CC combo remains dangerous in fights. In teamfights, keep your team spread to minimize Shockwave value and use R to block her engage.
edits.after: Nashor's Tooth makes soldier autos out-damage ball chip, and by two items your soldiers out-range her 815 Q outright. Command: Protect throws the ball to any ally at 1095 range, so a flank can arrive with Shockwave already in position — ward the angles rather than only watching her. Build MR if she has snowballed (Abyssal Mask). In fights keep your team spread past 410 so one Shockwave cannot gather it, and drop Emperor's Divide between that pile and her team.

notes: Orianna is female; the shipped page used he/his/him in eleven fields. Packet defect confirmed (sequencingCues 0): the page repeated 'track the ball position like a second enemy' four times without ever saying what the ball does. Now stated from Riot's text: Shockwave launches enemies TOWARD the ball, needs only 410 range, and Command: Protect can deliver the ball to any ally at 1095 — which is how a Shockwave arrives from a flank. The concrete sequencing line the packet asked for is the ball-stays-where-it-lands rule: step up when she Qs the wave, leave before her 7-second Q returns. Level chart disagreed across layers on six of seven rows (full: Skill x5, Azir, Skill; content and packet: Orianna x5, Azir, Azir); full moved to match, with every flipped row's why rewritten in the same proposal. NOT asserted anywhere: whether dashing or Flashing during Shockwave's delay escapes the pull, and whether Sand Soldiers absorb Command: Attack — neither is in the kit text. Ratings left untouched; their semantics are inconsistent across this champion's matchups.
